items.author: deavgprime
items.summary: It drops that parameter and any later parameters. If the string also contains, the parser returns an additional call named even though that text belongs to the original argument.
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

The Qwen3-Coder tool parser treats `</function>` inside a string parameter as the end of the outer function. It drops that parameter and any later parameters. If the string also contains `<function=other></function>`, the parser returns an additional call named `other` even though that text belongs to the original argument.

This can change file contents or commands returned by the generation server before an agent or evaluator receives them. I reproduced the parser output only; I did not execute any generated tool calls.

items.title: [Feat] pp: Replay breakable prefill graphs on PP stages with zigzag prefill CP
items.author: garry569
items.summary: Pipeline parallelism combined with prefill context parallelism always fell back to eager prefill, even with. Main already supports breakable prefill graphs on PP stages via proxy tensors (#36248), and zigzag CP already runs each rank's CP-local body inside the…
items.body:
## Motivation

Pipeline parallelism combined with prefill context parallelism (`--pp-size > 1 --enable-prefill-cp`) always fell back to eager prefill, even with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`. Main already supports breakable prefill graphs on PP stages via proxy tensors (#36248), and zigzag CP already runs each rank's CP-local body inside the breakable graph and only gathers at the logits tail. ## Motivation

`MiniMaxH3SamplingParams._synthetic_warmup_target` takes only the aspect ratio from `--warmup-resolutions` and always warms up at the 768 short edge. The flag is meant to name the canvas the server will serve, so this has two effects:

- **32 GB recipe.** The cookbook passes `--warmup-resolutions 864x480`, so warmup runs at a 768 short edge: a larger canvas than the server serves, on the tightest card.
- **544x960 workload.** A server deployed for the common 544x960 workload (`--warmup-resolutions 960x544`) still warms at 768, so its first real request pays the first-shape cost.

## Motivation

With `--enable-kv-cache-sharding`, `PageInterleavePoolAllocator` is on the scheduler's critical path for every prefill batch and every KV release. Today its cost grows with the batch:

- `free()` selects each owner class with a boolean mask, which costs one host sync per class.

items.title: [Perf] minimax-h3: Skip attention for the packing's alignment rows in the Ulysses pipeline
items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Skips attention computation for padding/alignment rows in H3's Ulysses pipelined attention, eliminating redundant cuDNN launches and host overhead.
items.body:
## Motivation

H3 pads its packed sequence to a multiple of 64 per Ulysses rank, so a 1280x704 request attends `cu_seqlens [0, 33002, 33024]`. cuDNN SDPA's varlen runs each segment as its own call, so every pipelined head group ran the real rows, a copy into the output, a cuDNN call for the 22 alignment rows and a second copy. With 7 groups per layer that is 28 extra launches and their host work per block.

## Modifications

- The alignment rows only ever reach their own rows (attention keeps them in their own segment, everything else is row-wise), so group attention now attends the real rows

The auto group count keeps only groups whose attention call fills four waves of 128-row tiles. items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Widen EAGLE periodic SWA tails so a diverging sibling keeps its prefix-cache hit
items.author: untrall
items.summary: Fixes #64808 (fix option B from the issue): with EAGLE spec decoding and a positive, a request sharing a long prefix falls back a whole retention interval (16384 -> 8192 cached tokens in the reporter's repro) instead of hitting the cached segment tail.
items.body:
## Summary
Fixes #64808 (fix option B from the issue): with EAGLE spec decoding and a positive `--prefix-cache-retention-interval`, a request sharing a long prefix falls back a whole retention interval (16384 -> 8192 cached tokens in the reporter's repro) instead of hitting the cached segment tail.

## Root cause
`SlidingWindowManager.reachable_block_mask` places each periodic segment tail so its right edge sits on the aligned boundary block (the EAGLE peek block, `shift=1`). A sibling that diverges right after a segment boundary cannot use that peek block, so its sliding-window hit lands one

items.author: Rockyeast
items.summary: Fixes out-of-bounds read in fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule when grouped value heads (HV > H) use default beta=None by sizing beta from v instead of q.
items.body:
## Overview

`fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` builds its default `beta` from `q` (`[B, T, H]`), but the kernel reads `beta` per value head. With grouped value heads (`HV > H`, as in Qwen3.5/Qwen3-Next) and `beta=None`, it reads past the end of the tensor. This builds the default from `v` (`[B, T, HV]`) in the vendored FLA op and in the two GLM-5-Next copies of it. Same fix as upstream fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1610 (Comba, gated Oja, preconditioned GDN, merged) and fla-org/flash-linear-attention#1618 (this GDN op, open).

items.title: [Perf] model_executor: Write small forward metadata with fill kernels behind SGLANG_ENABLE_MLP_SYNC_METADATA_FILL
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Replaces pinned host-to-device copies of small forward metadata with a Triton fill kernel to avoid copy-engine contention with bulk DMA transfers like HiCache load-back.
items.body:
## Motivation

The forward's small per-batch metadata (the DP-attention token counts and their logprob counterpart, the extend sequence and prefix lengths, and the non-padded token count) reaches the device as pinned host-to-device copies. Those copies share the copy engine with bulk host-to-device DMA, so when a large transfer is queued ahead of them, for example a HiCache load-back with the `direct` io backend, the forward waits behind that transfer before it can start, even though the metadata itself is a handful of integers.

## Modifications

Behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_MLP_SYNC_METADATA_FILL`

items.title: [Fix] hicache: mlock pinned host buffers so page aging never scans them
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: keeps a host pool's pages resident for DMA, but it leaves them on the kernel's evictable LRU. Proactive reclaim (page aging) clears the accessed flag of every page it scans there, pinned or not.
items.body:
## Motivation

`cudaHostRegister` keeps a host pool's pages resident for DMA, but it leaves them on the kernel's evictable LRU. Proactive reclaim (page aging) clears the accessed flag of every page it scans there, pinned or not. On GPUs that read host memory through the CPU page tables (ATS), the device's next access to an aged page takes a page fault instead of a plain read, so host-to-device copies out of a HiCache host pool can fault page by page once the pool has been aged.

Locked pages sit on the unevictable LRU and are never scanned, so making mlock part of pinning removes those faults

items.author: amd-dlimpus
items.summary: Routes GLM-5.3-Flash mxfp4 MLA prefill to a native gfx950 kernel, eliminating costly bf16 unpacking and closing the 3-10% performance gap versus e4m3 KV caches.
items.body:
## Overview

With the `mxfp4_mla` KV cache, prefill and mixed (prefill + decode) steps of GLM-5.3-Flash run the sparse prefill kernel, which unpacks every gathered row to bf16 for each query. At 8K context that makes mxfp4 KV 3-10% slower than e4m3 end to end (#64121, #64323), almost all of it in prefill. The e4m3 and bf16 caches instead run AITER's `triton_sparse_mla_fwd`, which does not accept `mxfp4_mla`. This PR routes those steps to #64323's native gfx950 kernel, which reads the packed rows on the scaled MFMA.

request-count collective. An authenticated request-arrival notice can park
followers until the leader resumes the existing count/payload broadcast.

The proposal reuses the existing ZeroMqQueue, endpoint/port bootstrap, request
queue and MPI route. It adds no periodic polling loop or new dependency. It

items.author: seanbell
items.summary: The Qwen4Exp HyperConnection kernels and the PLE gate kernel compute each token row's address as with, so the product is evaluated in int32 and wraps once it exceeds 231 - 1. This widens the row index to int64 once per kernel.

## Overview

The Qwen4Exp HyperConnection kernels (`nvidia/ops/hc.py`, `amd/ops/hc.py`) and the PLE gate kernel (`common/ops/ple.py`) compute each token row's address as `ptr + row * stride` with `row = tl.program_id(0)`, so the product is evaluated in int32 and wraps once it exceeds 2**31 - 1. completion sites in the PyTorch executor: side-stream copy completion,
asynchronous-copy readiness, shared sampler completion, and intermediate
pipeline-stage completion.

The host must await GPU completion at these points. Creating those events with
`torch.cuda.Event(blocking=True)` allows the existing host synchronization to
sleep rather than busy-wait, without removing a synchronization or changing
the event record point, stream ordering, source snapshot, or sampling policy.

items.author: misha-chertushkin
items.summary: On the Triton attention backend, EAGLE target verification runs through. That is the prefill kernel: one program per (sequence, head) walks the whole prefix serially.
items.body:
## Motivation
On the Triton attention backend, EAGLE target verification runs through `extend_attention_fwd`. That is the prefill kernel: one program per (sequence, head) walks the whole prefix serially. `verify_splitkv_fwd` (#27382) replaces it at `topk == 1` with a split-KV (flash-decode) kernel. Two things keep that kernel from serving gpt-oss on NVIDIA:

1. The backend enables it only on AMD gfx95.
2. `can_handle()` rejects attention sinks, and gpt-oss has sinks in every layer.

This matters most on NVIDIA SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 50xx), where Triton is the default attention back

…al <tool_call> in Hermes streaming parser

When serving with --tool-call-parser hermes and stream=True, if the model output contains a literal <tool_call> in ordinary prose (e.g. explaining tool syntax or unclosed markup), the streaming parser held back all subsequent text tokens awaiting tool completion. Because no valid tool call was formed, this held-back buffer was never emitted, causing the streaming output to diverge from non-streaming.

This commit:

items.title: [Performance][ROCm]: set HSA_SCRATCH_SINGLE_LIMIT in the ROCm image: per-dispatch scratch allocation costs ~130 us before large RCCL all-reduces on MI355X
items.author: jbelofamd
items.summary: The cause is that the kernel's scratch need is over the runtime's single-dispatch limit. ROCr then allocates scratch for that dispatch and releases it afterwards, on every launch.
items.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

**Summary.** On MI355X, a TP8 serve pays about 130 us of GPU idle time in front of some RCCL all-reduces in prefill and mixed (prefill + decode) steps. The cause is that the kernel's scratch need is over the runtime's single-dispatch limit. ROCr then allocates scratch for that dispatch and releases it afterwards, on every launch. `HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1`, which `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` already sets, does not cover this case. Raising `HSA_SCRATCH_SINGLE_LIMIT` keeps the scratch resident: the gap goes to 0, the layer runs 7% faster, and end-to-end serv

## Summary
A leg's GitHub Actions runner can lose its connection after its servers come up, before `launch_mi355x.sh` reaches its own cleanup. On spur the servers run as detached docker containers, so they keep running -- holding GPU memory and the node allocation -- until the Slurm job's wall-clock limit, starving every other leg queued for the same shared node pool.

- `launch_mi355x.sh`: add an `EXIT`/`INT`/`TERM` trap that reaps the leg's containers and cancels its Slurm job, so a killed/disconnected runner no longer leaves them running indefinitely.

items.title: Start a chunked prefill only when its whole prompt fits
items.author: lmcafee-nvidia
items.summary: With chunked prefill enabled, the dynamic engine can stop making progress under KV-cache pressure, and never returns. lets a new request start a chunked prefill when the KV cache has room for one prompt token.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With chunked prefill enabled, the dynamic engine can stop making progress
under KV-cache pressure, and `generate()` never returns.
`_can_schedule_chunked_prefill()` lets a new request start a chunked
prefill when the KV cache has room for one prompt token. A long prompt can
therefore start, take the last free blocks, and then wait for one more
block. A partial chunked prefill keeps its blocks until it finishes and is
never preempted. Requests decoding beside it then pause for want of a
block. If they hold no more blocks than the paused-block budget, nothing is
evicted

items.title: [Fix] [AMD] scheduler: Keep the scheduler's GPU work on the forward stream under monokernel
items.author: zijiecode
items.summary: An AMD monokernel launch (, sgl-amd-mono) keeps all of its workgroups resident and waiting on each other through device-memory flags. The overlap scheduler issues small kernels on its own, and the result readback runs on.
items.body:
## Motivation

An AMD monokernel launch (`--enable-amd-monokernel`, sgl-amd-mono) keeps all of its workgroups resident and waiting on each other through device-memory flags. The overlap scheduler issues small kernels on its own `schedule_stream`, and the result readback runs on `copy_stream`. If one of those kernels takes a CU while a monokernel launch is being dispatched, some of the launch's workgroups cannot become resident. The resident ones then wait until the plugin's guard deadline (60 s) stops every rank, and the log shows a GPU memory fault at address `(nil)`.

## Description

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4/FP8 checkpoints store the PLE n-gram table as FP8 e4m3 plus a scalar
scale, and the table stays FP8 until after lookup. With attention DP and `tp_size > 1`, each rank
owns a row slice of the table: it all-gathers every rank's n-gram IDs, looks up the rows it owns,
zeroes the rest, dequantizes, and reduce-scatters. The zeroing ran on the still-FP8 rows, and
PyTorch has no FP8 `masked_fill_` kernel, so every worker failed in its first forward (warmup):

NotImplementedError: "masked_fill_" not implemented for 'Float8_e4m3fn'

When the Hugging Face cache already holds a snapshot of the model that has a tokenizer, the Rust frontend reads every model file from that snapshot and never contacts the Hub. The per-step LoRA metadata path is slow on the CPU and blocks on the GPU:

items.title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 outputs turn into `!!!!` (token 0) streams under load (FlashKDA spreads one NaN across requests; FlashMLA SM90 decode PDL race)
items.author: simon-veitner-redhat
items.summary: NaN activations in one request propagate via FlashKDA prefill to other batched requests, compounded by a suspected SM90 decode race in FlashMLA, causing multi-request output corruption under heavy KV-cache load.
items.body:
### In short

Under heavy load, some Kimi-K3 requests stop producing text and emit token id 0 (`!`) until `max_tokens`. Behind each `!` is a NaN logit.
It starts when one request's activations go NaN for a single step. The leading suspect is a race in FlashMLA's SM90 decode kernel (not proven).
A FlashKDA prefill kernel then copies that NaN into other requests of the same batch (confirmed), so one bad request becomes 10 or more.
In one eval run this cost 56 of 516 reasoning outputs and dropped AIME25 from 0.883 to 0.700.
With fixes for both kernels, our reproducer showed no bad request.

### W

items.author: Denji-kk

items.title: [Fix] disaggregation: Settle the in-flight decode result before a PD decode retraction
items.author: Denji-kk
items.summary: With overlap scheduling, a PD decode worker can retract a request while the previous decode step's result is still queued. The retraction backs up the request's device state and requeues the request.
items.body:
## Motivation

With overlap scheduling, a PD decode worker can retract a request while the previous decode step's result is still queued. The retraction backs up the request's device state and requeues the request. On resume, the backup is restored and the request decodes from `output_ids`.

By the time the backup is taken, the device state has already taken the in-flight step, but `output_ids` has not. Result processing skips retracted requests, so the in-flight step never reaches `output_ids`. The backup and `output_ids` end up one step apart:

- **Speculative decoding:** the in-flight verif

## Motivation

At trace level 3, SGLang emits a `decode_loop` span for **every** decode step of every
request. For long generations (thousands of tokens) this produces one span per token per

drop spans, and the tracing backend becomes unusable in production. Users therefore have to
choose between level 3 (full detail, unusable volume) and level 2 (no per-step detail at all).

This PR adds `SGLANG_TRACE_DECODE_MAX_STEPS` so operators can trace only the first N decode
steps per request — enough to diagnose

items.body: This model has a token whose top-k MoE router logits are nearly tied. Both vLLM and HF accumulate bf16 rounding noise of similar magnitude, and at this tie that noise can push either side to pick a different expert, which shifts the token's softmax past the tolerance. The default bf16 HF reference happens to land on the opposite side of the tie from vLLM here, while vLLM's bf16 selection agrees with the fp32 result. Compare against an fp32 HF reference so the golden value sits on the well-defined fp32 side of the tie instead of an unstable bf16 one.

In WRITE mode, `MoRIIOConnector` assumes one prefill rank per TP index that writes every layer. Each stage also numbers its layers from zero, so a stage that does write puts them on the decode instance's first layers. ## Overview

For a Responses `custom` tool, every streamed argument delta re-runs `partial_json_parser` over the whole accumulated arguments, so the API server's cost per delta grows with the tool input. This decodes only the new tail of the input string. Follow-up to #57322.

items.body:
## Overview

When a tool call repeats a key whose value was already streamed, `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta` fails the prefix check before it installs the argument value extender. Every later delta then re-converts the whole argument text, only to fail the same check, so the API server's cost per token grows with the call. ## Overview

The Rust frontend returns a bare 404 for `/ping` and `/invocations`. The Python frontend always registers both for SageMaker (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/sagemaker/api_router.py`), and SageMaker health-checks a container through `/ping`, so a SageMaker deployment with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` never comes up healthy.

This serves `GET`/`POST /ping` with the existing `/health` handler, which is what Python does and what the Rust render server already does (`routes/render.rs`). `/invocations` gets the standard 501 placeholder the router uses for other Python routes it doesn't implement

items.title: [None][fix] Reject variable-width beam search under overlap
items.author: jongukc
items.summary: With the overlap scheduler, two concurrent requests whose widens (for example ) can read KV that no forward wrote. To keep the batch width uniform, the scheduler skips one request for an iteration while its generation position still advances.
items.body:
Under the overlap scheduler, concurrent requests that widen through beam_width_array can be skipped for one iteration to keep the batch width uniform while their generation position still advances. Their next attention step then reads a KV position that no forward wrote. Reject a changing beam_width_array at request validation when overlap is enabled; constant arrays and disable_overlap_scheduler=True are unaffected. Document the restriction.

items.title: [Bugfix][SleepMode] Exact-size, reusable pinned CPU backup for level-1 sleep
items.author: aoshen02
items.summary: Replaces power-of-two-rounded cached pinned allocations with exact-size reusable CPU backup tensors, reducing level-1 sleep host memory overhead from ~2x to actual offloaded size.
items.body:
## Problem

Level-1 sleep backs up every cumem allocation to host memory with `torch.empty(size, pin_memory=True)`. torch's `CachingHostAllocator` rounds each pinned block up to a power of two and keeps freed blocks in its cache, so the level-1 backup costs up to ~2x the offloaded bytes in host memory, and that memory is never returned to the OS. On Mistral Large 4 at TP8 the backup is 85.19 GiB per GPU, which turned into roughly +578 GiB of host memory per node.

## Root cause

The backup size is chosen by the caching host allocator, not by the allocation. The old code already kept the memory

items.summary: V1 configures trainer and standalone rollout pools separately. On two 8-GPU nodes, that interface cannot describe a rollout pool occupying one full node and half of the other while leaving the remaining four GPUs to the trainer.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

V1 `separate_async` configures trainer and standalone rollout pools separately.
On two 8-GPU nodes, that interface cannot describe a rollout pool occupying one
full node and half of the other while leaving the remaining four GPUs to the
trainer. This change adds an opt-in `shared_rollout_gpus` setting: the physical
pool is reserved once and split into disjoint rollout and trainer bundles. For
example, `trainer.nnodes=2 trainer.n_gpus_per_node=8` and
`trainer.v1.separate_async.shared_rollout_gpus=12` assign 12 GPUs to rollout and
4 to training; setting it to 10 yields

[NVBug 6854801](https://nvbugs/6854801) tracks silent disaggregated stages. The launcher prints a heartbeat every ten minutes even when benchmark logs are missing, unreadable, or stalled. That prevents the watchdog from detecting a real hang.

items.body:
NVFP4_PLUS keeps the E2M1 values of NVFP4 but stores one UE5M3 block scale per 32 values and has no FP32 per-tensor scale. The SM107 block-scaled MMA (kind::mxf4nvf4) reads UE5M3 scales directly, and UE5M3 spans 2^-17 to 114688, so activation blocks need no global normalization.

## Root cause

The FlashInfer activation-quantization tactic passed the SF-layout request as `do_shuffle`. In the pinned FlashInfer 0.6.18 API, that option permutes matrix rows and applies weight-scale shuffling; it is independent of `sfLayout`. ## Fix

- Select `SfLayout.layout_128x4` or `SfLayout.layout_linear` explicitly and keep activation rows unshuffled.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8433.

`SFTTrainer` built its train/val `StatefulDataLoader`s without a `generator`, so every iterator construction drew a `base_seed` from the global CPU RNG. This PR gives each dataloader its own seeded `torch.Generator`, so building iterators no longer touches the global CPU RNG and the restored state is the one training actually continues with.

## Description

`trtllm-serve disaggregated` with `num_workers > 1` and no external coordinator URL runs the coordinator in the launcher process. By default (`TRTLLM_DISAGG_COORDINATOR_UDS=1`) it serves the co-located fleet over a Unix domain socket, next to its TCP listener on `port - 1`.

Before this change, `_serve_coordinator_and_fleet` created that socket at the fixed path `/tmp/trtllm_disagg_coord_<port>.sock`, directly in `/tmp`, and uvicorn sets mode `0666` on the socket file it binds. The socket file stayed in `/tmp` after the coordinator exited.

Now the socket is `coordinator.sock`

items.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Batch-invariant inference at TP=2 reduces the sequence-parallel partials with a symmetric-memory pull kernel instead of an NCCL reduce-scatter. The result is bitwise NCCL's, which is what training uses, and each decode step is about 0.3 ms faster.

## Details

At TP=2 every reduced element is a single addition, so its order cannot vary. Batch-invariant mode still turned off the NVLS path for the row-parallel and sequence-parallel reduce-scatters and used NCCL, because the NVLS `multimem.ld_reduce`

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

-

Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

### What does this PR do?

Adds experimental teacher-generated rollouts for distillation. A user function chooses the student or teacher once per training batch; the existing teacher server generates teacher responses and scores the completed sequences. Validation always uses the student. With no selector, training keeps its existing behavior.

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

`ReplayBuffer._wait_for_next_poll()` sleeps a hard-coded `poll_interval=2.0` between TransferQueue metadata syncs (used
by both the sync `sample()` and the async `wait_for_sampleable()`). The trainer therefore notices the last finished
prompt up to 2 s late, and `timing_s/gen` is quantized to multiples of 2 s (main, vLLM: 2.21, 4.21, 4.21, 2.21 … s;
SGLang: 2.28 s every step). This PR replaces the sleep with a wait on a small completion counter that rollout workers
bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

### What does this PR do?

Megatron's `optimizer_cpu_offload=True` turns the optimizer into a **HybridDeviceOptimizer (HDO)**: it permanently splits optimizer state between CPU memory and GPU memory via `optimizer_offload_fraction`. …he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. Nothing in training then keeps the actor's probability on those ids in check, and it can drift freely since they are never sampled and never penalized.

items.author: yph22
items.summary: Honor when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation. Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.author: ruizhang0101
items.summary: Megatron does not look those functions up at call time. Three modules bind them when they are imported: -:,, -:, -: imports at module level and applies the patch later, in, so Megatron keeps the unpatched originals.
items.body:
Fixes #2452.

## Problem

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ

## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.title: fix: reject non-positive rollout temperature at parse time
items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.
items.body:
## Problem

`--rollout-temperature 0` is greedy decoding. That is not a usable on-policy RL policy: the sampling distribution is a delta, while log-probs (and PPO ratios) still come from a softmax. Greedy RL should be rejected at config parse, not assumed away in loss code.

`--eval-temperature 0` is unchanged; greedy eval remains valid.

## Change

`slime_validate_args` raises if `rollout_temperature <= 0`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_megatron_argument_validation.py` — `0.0` and `-0.1` raise; existing validate-args cases still pass at the default `1.0`

## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution.
